subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should OpenClaw broaden NO_REPLY suppression for mixed trailing or own-line payloads, and where should the boundary sit between silent-intent internal text and legitimate substantive replies that mention or append the token?
rationale: Current main deliberately preserves some substantive trailing-token replies, while the issue asks for broader suppression to avoid internal text leaks; that changes shared message-delivery and security semantics rather than a mechanical cleanup.

options.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
options.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies across all delivery paths.

options.title: Use blanket trailing or own-line suppression
options.body: Suppress any reply ending with a trailing or own-line NO_REPLY token, accepting that some currently visible substantive replies may be dropped.

options.title: Keep the current narrow policy
options.body: Document that only token-only, punctuation-only, and reasoning-prefixed silent payloads are suppressed, then close or retarget broad suppression requests.

recommendation.title: Adopt classifier-based suppression
recommendation.body: Define a shared classifier that suppresses internal or silent-intent mixed payloads while preserving legitimate substantive replies across all delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They closed the adjacent punctuation-token issue and are the best available routing candidate for a cross-cutting delivery-policy choice from the owners identified here.
